2.translation: Extract the [input bundle](⟦shared:0⟧) so the working directory contains examples/. Each section names its optional dependencies.

4.translation: Use ⟦shared:0⟧ to retain characters with their physical header line and optional file provenance. Only whitespace is removed; case is retained. Declare bp or aa explicitly instead of guessing the alphabet. Focusing crops the string as well as the interval; local position 1 below is original position 1001. A decreasing locus selects the same interval and does not reverse-complement it. Lengths alone cannot supply characters; HSP endpoints cannot supply mismatch or gap columns. Gapped FASTA counts gap characters and needs a separate alignment-to-source map before genomic use.

6.translation: ## Existing alignments: keep columns and source positions separate ⟦shared:0⟧

7.translation: These examples require the source checkout's ⟦shared:0⟧ directory. It contains unchanged Biopython DNA/protein alignment inputs, the upstream permission notice, hashes and a reproducible FASTA re-encoding rule. No aligner is run. Full record IDs and original characters remain unchanged; choose rows and columns explicitly.

8.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ reads one existing alignment. Declare DNA, RNA or AA; equal lengths alone do not establish homology. ⟦shared:1⟧ includes ⟦shared:2⟧ and ⟦shared:3⟧ gaps, whose ⟦shared:4⟧ is NA. Default positions count the ungapped input fragment from one; they are not complete-genome coordinates. Lowercase letters consume positions, so this reader must not be used as an A3M insertion parser.

10.translation: The first selected row has a gap at alignment column 343. Column lookup therefore returns ⟦shared:0⟧, ⟦shared:1⟧ and a missing source position. Inverse lookup of source position 343 finds its actual alignment column, without interpolation. Positions removed by filtering return ⟦shared:2⟧; filtering never renumbers retained columns. ⟦shared:3⟧ selects an alignment-row ID even when a separately declared source ID differs.

11.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ is a standard Cartesian ggplot layer. Styles and user scales follow ggplot2. It measures glyphs against actual cell width and height at draw time: ⟦shared:1⟧ requires readable letters; ⟦shared:2⟧ retains colour cells where text cannot fit, without shrinking fonts. Focus fewer columns or increase physical width to show letters. For example, save ⟦shared:4⟧ with ordinary ⟦shared:3⟧; simply raising DPI adds no physical room. Discrete rows, identity/reverse position scales and Cartesian coordinates are supported; this layer does not directly project characters onto backbone Coords. A Cartesian character plot with explicit source mapping can be registered using ⟦shared:5⟧ for [Fusion character details](⟦shared:6⟧).

13.translation: The same data contract accepts actual protein characters. This excerpt contains upstream gaps and residue differences; fill distinguishes literal symbols, not inferred functional domains.

16.translation: Provide one ⟦shared:0⟧ row per aligned record with ⟦shared:1⟧, ⟦shared:2⟧ and ⟦shared:3⟧. ⟦shared:2⟧ is the first nongap source coordinate. Negative-strand positions decrease; strings must already be in alignment orientation. An optional ⟦shared:4⟧ identifies the original molecule. If you provide a full forward ⟦shared:5⟧, every nongap character is checked, using nucleotide complementation on the negative strand and order reversal only for AA. Missing source strings remain unverified; no origins or strands are guessed.

17.translation: The following example checks consistency against ungapped fragments derived from the same alignment. It is deliberately **not independent genomic validation**. For a real genomic projection, supply independently known source sequences and interval metadata instead.

19.translation: No mismatch/gap detail can be recovered from six HSP endpoints alone. This workflow accepts existing columns, not CIGAR/A3M/Clustal/Stockholm parsing, phase inference, consensus/Logo analysis or alignment computation. Explicit CDS translation is described below; exact macro/detail registration is available in the Fusion section.

21.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ defines observed coding coordinates; ⟦shared:1⟧ additionally needs actual complete forward DNA/RNA strings and optional **Biostrings**. This real EMALE negative-strand CDS has source phase 0 and an ATG start. Table 11 is an explicit choice checked against the unchanged upstream protein FASTA. Input provenance is in ⟦shared:2⟧.

23.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ reports coding/protein strings, genetic code, initiation/ambiguity policies, partial ends and terminal remainder. ⟦shared:1⟧ retains each genomic base; ⟦shared:2⟧ contains the three genomic positions of each codon in biological order, even across exon boundaries. Residue positions use the CDS feature ID's observed-protein namespace; they are not an inferred external protein accession. Terminal and internal stops remain ⟦shared:3⟧. The example removes only the final stop for comparison with the upstream FASTA convention.

24.translation: The default ⟦shared:0⟧ does not recode alternative starts; ⟦shared:1⟧ requires a complete 5-prime end. ⟦shared:2⟧ rejects fuzzy codons; explicit ⟦shared:3⟧ delegates to Biostrings, using X if unresolved. Unknown codes, missing/short sources and declared translation exceptions fail. ⟦shared:4⟧ belongs to the CDS map: only the initial phase and incomplete terminal codon are excluded; later segment phases validate continuity without deleting junction bases. No missing sequence is reconstructed. RNA must be declared explicitly. Ordered ⟦shared:5⟧ support the existing spliced/origin-join contract.

25.translation: A complete runnable nucleotide/codon/macro example is ⟦shared:0⟧; its negative-strand labels are centred on their three coding bases. Real spliced plus/minus controls, source hashes and original expected translations are retained in ⟦shared:1⟧. [Register the character plot](⟦shared:2⟧) to connect its exact source boundaries.
